# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish communication and share what I see, since I can only speak to Mute and Blind (both hear me), but I need to wait for Mute to relay manual info. Let me share my observations now since Blind can hear me directly too.

```
speak(text="I see: display shows 3, light is green, wires are 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute gestured 🤟 to me. I can't hear speech from Mute, only see gestures. This is likely Mute trying to signal something using a pre-agreed or intuitive meaning, but since we have no established code yet, I should treat this as an acknowledgment or attempt to communicate a category. I don't have enough information to interpret it definitively yet, so I'll wait and see if more context or gestures clarify, while continuing to relay my bomb details to Blind.

```
speak(text="Repeating what I see: display 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green. Mute, I received a gesture from you but cannot hear your words.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute keeps sending the same gesture 🤟 to me. Since gestures have no pre-defined meaning, Mute might be trying to ask me something specific, or acknowledge receipt, or trying to build a code. Since I can't hear Mute's speech, and Mute cannot hear me but can only gesture to me and speak to Blind... wait, let me reconsider the channels.

Actually, re-reading: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So Blind receives my speech too. But does Mute's speech reach me? No - "You never receive speech" as Deaf. So Mute can speak to Blind, but I never hear it. Mute can only gesture to me, and I can see gestures.

Since Mute repeats 🤟 twice, this might just be a fixed acknowledgment or a request for repetition. I'll continue relaying full bomb details since that's my main value, and try a distinct gesture back isn't possible for me (I don't gesture, I speak/see). Let me just keep speaking the bomb state for Blind's benefit, since Blind needs my visual info via my speech.

```
speak(text="Bomb state unchanged: display 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green. Blind, please act based on manual instructions from Mute combined with this.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute keeps sending exactly the same single gesture 🤟 every turn, with no variation. This suggests it might not be meaningful new information but rather something automatic, or Mute is stuck waiting for something from me since gestures alone can't convey complex manual instructions.

Since Mute cannot speak to me (I never receive speech) and can only gesture to me, and gestures are quite limited for conveying complex manual text, Mute may be trying to establish a simple signal-based protocol. Since I have no way to ask Mute questions (Mute can't hear my speech either... wait, can Mute hear? Let me check - Mute "cannot speak" but nothing says Mute cannot hear. Looking at the table: Mute "Can: Read the manual" "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb". So Mute CAN hear speech and CAN see? No - only Deaf can see. Mute cannot see gestures neither since only "whoever can see" receives gestures, and only Deaf can see.

So Mute can hear my speech! That's the channel. I've been speaking, and Mute has been receiving it, but only gesturing back since Mute cannot speak. Mute is likely trying to give me a signal via gesture since that's the only channel back to me from Mute.

A single repeated gesture might mean "yes" or "correct" or "continue" - acknowledging my reports. Since the state hasn't changed and Mute keeps confirming the same thing, this could mean the current wire/light/display state matches something safe or expected in the manual. Let me try encoding a question via gesture-like distinct speech, and ask Blind to try touching wire 3 (green) since it matches the light color, as a common bomb-defusal convention - but I should be cautious without more protocol.

Let me instead propose using gestures as a shared code - since I can't gesture (only speak/see), I need Blind to relay to Mute via speech, and Mute relays back to me via gesture only. Let me ask Blind to ask Mute specific questions and relay Mute's spoken answer to me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, can you hear Mute speak? If so, please ask Mute what action to take given display 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green, and tell me what Mute says.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute continues sending 🤟 consistently. Blind hasn't spoken back to me (I wouldn't hear it anyway - wait, I never receive speech from anyone, including Blind). So even if Blind answers Mute's instructions, I would never hear it since "You never receive speech" as Deaf applies to all speech, not just from specific people.

This means my only channel of incoming information is gestures (from Mute, since only Mute can gesture... actually Blind can't gesture since Blind can't see either, and can't make gestures meaningfully since gestures are visual signals - but wait, Blind can still physically make gestures, they just can't see them. Let me reconsider: the constraint is about receiving, not sending. Blind could gesture but wouldn't know what they're making since they can't see. Actually nothing stops Blind from gesturing arbitrarily, but that's not useful since Blind can't coordinate visually.)

So functionally: I receive gestures only from Mute (the one who can direct gestures meaningfully, since Mute can hear my speech and respond with intentional gestures). I speak to Mute and Blind. Blind speaks to Mute and Deaf... wait no, "you never receive speech" - that's my restriction. Let's check Blind's channels aren't stated to me directly, but the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - meaning Blind speaks and Mute+Deaf can potentially receive.

Given Mute keeps repeating 🤟 exactly, and nothing changes, perhaps this gesture simply means "acknowledged, proceed" or "correct, continue" - a confirmation signal. Since the bomb state hasn't changed and no danger indicated, maybe Mute is confirming everything is fine to proceed with whatever default/safe action is. Given light is GREEN (often "go/safe" in conventional signaling) and wire 3 matches light color green, this seems like a strong candidate.

I should propose a concrete action to Blind directly, since Blind can act.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute keeps confirming with the same gesture each turn, suggesting agreement. Given light is green and wire 3 is also green, I believe cutting or acting on wire 3 matches the manual's expected action. Proceed with wire 3 if your instructions align, but wait for Mute's explicit guidance if possible.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute continues the identical single gesture every single turn with zero variation, across 5 turns now, despite the bomb state never changing either. This strongly suggests this is simply a fixed/default gesture Mute is producing - possibly Mute has no way to encode variable information via gesture alone and is just doing something like "hello" or a placeholder, or perhaps Mute genuinely has nothing more specific to signal to me and this is a constant "standby" indicator.

Given the stalemate, I should try a different approach: give Blind very explicit, complete information so Blind (who can act and presumably hears both Mute's spoken manual info and can combine it with what I relay) can make the final call. Since Blind is the one who acts, and Blind should be able to hear Mute directly (per turn order Mute->Blind->Deaf, Blind receives Mute's speech).

I'll keep relaying full bomb state consistently to help Blind cross-reference with the manual Mute is reading aloud to Blind.

```
speak(text="Full bomb status, unchanged over multiple turns: DISPLAY shows 3, LIGHT is green, WIRES are 1-blue, 2-yellow, 3-green. Blind, please combine this with whatever Mute has told you from the manual to decide the correct action.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute changed the gesture pattern from a single 🤟 to three ☝ symbols. This is a meaningful change! Three repetitions of ☝ (index finger pointing up) could be encoding the number 3 - possibly pointing to "wire 3" or confirming the "display 3" value, or indicating "cut wire 3" as a count-based code.

Given that display shows 3 and wire 3 is green (matching light color), this gesture of three ☝ symbols strongly suggests Mute is confirming or pointing to "3" - likely wire 3, since that's the actionable item. This aligns with my earlier hypothesis to Blind about wire 3.

I should relay this new gesture information to Blind immediately, as it seems to be a confirmation signal about the number 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just changed their gesture to three repetitions of a pointing-up sign, likely encoding the number 3. This matches both the display value and wire 3, which is green like the light. I believe this confirms: act on wire 3.")
wait()
```
